body:
Found while fixing #565.

PMID 33592498 (PMC8724627) curates three parental (CIITA-negative) arms, all `mhc_class: "I"`, and three CIITA-transduced class-II arms. But the deposit carries class-II rows under the parental-only elution statements:

| deposited statement | class I | class II |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| `... HRGO02 cells.` | 739 | 152 |
| `... HROG17 cells.` | 1208 | 401 |
| `... RA cells.` | 839 | 32 |

585 class-II rows in total, and the paper agrees they exist: *"As GBM cells do not naturally express HLA-II molecules, only 165, 651, and 83 peptides were identified in HROG02, HROG17, and RA cells, respectively. The majority of them were not predicted to bind the respective HLA-II allotypes ... suggesting that a background level of potential contaminants contributed to these identifications."*

With #565 merged these rows land in one of two wrong-ish places:

- on an allele typed in only one line (e.g. `HLA-DRB1*01:02`) the allele join hands them to that line's **CIITA-transduced** class-II arm, so a peptide eluted from untransduced cells is reported as coming from a transduced sample;
- on an allele shared between lines (`HLA-DRB4*01:03`, `HLA-DPA1*01:03/DPB1*04:01`) `elution_condition_ids` maps the statement to the parental class-I arm, which is not a candidate, so 93 rows reach no arm at all.

Two possible resolutions, neither obviously right without a decision on how the corpus should treat authors' own contaminant calls:

- [ ] curate three parental class-II arms so these rows attribute to the sample they were actually eluted from, and record the paper's own assessment that most are background rather than true ligands; or
- [ ] decide these rows are not evidence of presentation and exclude them, which needs a general rule, not a per-study one.

The study's `arm_resolution` stays `curation_gap` for exactly this reason (its note was updated in #565).

https://claude.ai/code/session_01UosikwXjt2X2cX2cisMAjc
title: PMID 33592498 has no parental class-II arm for 585 deposited HLA-II rows
